edges.effect_quant: The strongest quantitative studies point in a harmful direction, but the pooled magnitude varies across populations and methods.
edges.mechanism: B12 deficiency impairs myelin maintenance, which is why sensory neuropathy is one of its most recognizable neurologic consequences.
edges.summary: The strongest piece here is the 2025 Hamza Ali systematic review in Cureus, which ties vitamin b12 deficiency to peripheral neuropathy in a direction that later studies largely support. That makes this edge more about calibrating magnitude and context than arguing over whether the signal exists at all.
edges.caveats: Residual confounding and reverse causation remain possible in some observational studies, so the main readout is direction and plausibility rather than one exact risk number.

evidence.notes: The Neurological Sequelae of Vitamin B12 Deficiency: A Systematic Review and Randomized Controlled Trial.
